newsitem.title: USA: Humana has higher first quarter earnings.
newsitem.headline: Humana has higher first quarter earnings.

text.p: Humana Inc. Tuesday reported lower first quarter earnings, hurt by declines in commercial membership.

The health care company said commercial membership decreased by 113,400 during the quarter. This decline was due to the company's change in product pricing begun in the fall of 1996 and withdrawal from certain unprofitable markets, it said.

"We've made great strides in eliminating our unprofitable business by selling operations or exiting certain markets and pricing our products more appropriately. We have a lot of work ahead, however, in terms of implementing improved medical management processes," said Gregory H. Wolf, Humana's president and chief operating officer.
Human had first-quarter earnings of $39 million, or 24 cents a share, compared with $53 million, or 32 cents a share, a year earlier. Revenues were $1.8 billion, up from $1.56 billion in 1996.

Revenue growth was based in part on revenues earned from its Civilian Health and Medical Programme of the Uniformed Services contract as well as premium rate increases in its commercial and Medicare risk products.
During the quarter, the healthcare company also completed the purchase of Health Direct, Inc. for $23 million in cash.
This transaction added more than 50,000 members to Humana's Chicago medical membership, which now totals approximately 648,000.
Humana, headquartered in Louisville, Ky., has more than 4.8 million health plan members primarily located in 17 states.
Humana stock was up 50 cents at $20.75 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exhange.
